summary: The milestone completed 11 experiments in 29.1 minutes, including 6 compute-bound experiments. The 22.69-minute provenance-complete fixed-policy corpus v2 set the execution tail, while the locked task-level GPU-idle indicator remained false.
bottlenecks_identified: The provenance-complete fixed-policy corpus v2 consumed 22.69 of 29.1 minutes. Its label identifies a canary-readiness dependency, but the data does not separate readiness wait, setup, inference, or persistence time.

Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks experiment duration but does not provide task-scoped phase or GPU telemetry. The cause of the compute tail and the efficiency of accelerator use therefore cannot be measured.
improvements_suggested: Add a readiness-aware preflight that records gate evaluation separately and lets the scheduler run independent ready work while a dependency remains unresolved.
Record phase boundaries and task-scoped GPU samples from experiment start through completion so waiting time can be separated from accelerator work.
Record loaded-model concurrency and runner selection for each compute task. Select DualGPURunner only when two or more models run in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Separate readiness checks from measured execution and dispatch other ready work during unresolved gates.
Add experiment-linked phase timing and GPU duty-cycle receipts.
Add model-count and runner-selection receipts, with DualGPURunner routing for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The available data identifies the tail but does not establish its internal cause, compute-period GPU efficiency, or parallel model loading. A defensible savings rate cannot be calculated from this single reconstructed run, so the estimate remains zero.
